sentences.text: On most trains, each pair of wheels is locked to one solid steel axle, so both wheels always turn together.

sentences.text: But on a bend, the outer wheel has farther to go.

sentences.text: So why doesn't one of them skid?

sentences.text: The outer rail is about two point four meters longer either way.

sentences.text: And a one-hundred-ton locomotive has nothing to fix that.

sentences.tagged: No steering, no differential gears, the box that lets your car's outer wheel spin faster.

sentences.text: Yet on a gentle curve, if you could watch the wheels, you would see that neither one really slips.

sentences.text: The answer is in the shape of the wheel, and you've probably never noticed it.

sentences.text: And that same shape explains the screech you hear on a tight bend, and why fast trains sway.

sentences.text: So what steers it?

sentences.text: The steel lips on the inside of each wheel, the flanges?

sentences.text: That is what you would probably guess.
sentences.tagged: That is what you would probably guess.

sentences.text: But here is the surprise.
sentences.tagged: But here is the surprise.

sentences.text: On a gentle curve, the flanges do not need to touch the rail at all.
sentences.tagged: On a gentle curve, the flanges do not need to touch the rail at all.

sentences.text: Look closely at the tread, the part of the wheel that rolls on the rail.
sentences.tagged: Look closely at the tread, the part of the wheel that rolls on the rail.

sentences.text: Do you see it?
sentences.tagged: Do you see it?

sentences.text: It is not flat.

sentences.text: It is tapered, close to a cone, so the wheel gets slightly bigger toward the flange.
sentences.tagged: It is tapered, close to a cone, so the wheel gets slightly bigger toward the flange.

sentences.text: The slope is about one in twenty.
sentences.tagged: The slope is about one in twenty.

sentences.text: If you move twenty millimeters across, its radius grows by one millimeter.
sentences.tagged: If you move twenty millimeters across, its radius grows by one millimeter.

sentences.text: Now watch the axle enter a curve.
sentences.tagged: Now watch the axle enter a curve.

sentences.text: With both wheels the same size, it rolls straight on.
sentences.tagged: With both wheels the same size, it rolls straight on.

sentences.text: But the rails bend away beneath it, so it drifts a few millimeters toward the outside of the bend.
sentences.tagged: But the rails bend away beneath it, so it drifts a few millimeters toward the outside of the bend.

sentences.text: And now you have the trick.

sentences.text: That moves the outer wheel onto its fatter part, near the flange, and the inner wheel onto its thinner part, away from its flange.
sentences.tagged: That moves the outer wheel onto its fatter part, near the flange, and the inner wheel onto its thinner part, away from its flange.

sentences.text: So the outer wheel rolls on a bigger circle, and the inner wheel on a smaller one.
sentences.tagged: So the outer wheel rolls on a bigger circle, and the inner wheel on a smaller one.

sentences.text: Same spin, different distance.

sentences.text: It keeps drifting until the outer wheel is just big enough to cover the extra distance.
sentences.tagged: It keeps drifting until the outer wheel is just big enough to cover the extra distance.

sentences.text: Now neither wheel really slips, and the axle follows the curve by itself.

sentences.text: How big is that difference?

sentences.tagged: Take the textbook version, two wheels and their axle, which engineers call a wheelset.

sentences.text: If you shift it as far as it can go, its two wheels differ in radius by about seven tenths of a millimeter.

sentences.text: It even works on straight track.

sentences.text: Imagine you nudge the axle to one side.

sentences.text: The wheel on that side gets bigger, so the axle steers itself back toward the middle.

sentences.text: But shape has a limit.

sentences.tagged: The textbook wheelset you just saw can only shift about seven millimeters before the flange meets the rail.

sentences.text: Any tighter, and the flange starts to touch the rail.
sentences.tagged: Any tighter, and the flange starts to touch the rail.

sentences.text: And on a really tight curve?
sentences.tagged: And on a really tight curve?

sentences.text: The flange presses hard against the rail and drags the axle round, but at a slight angle.
sentences.tagged: The flange presses hard against the rail and drags the axle round, but at a slight angle.

sentences.text: So the tread is scraped sideways across the top of the rail.
sentences.tagged: So the tread is scraped sideways across the top of the rail.

sentences.text: And that is the screech you hear.
sentences.tagged: And that is the screech you hear.

sentences.text: You would think it is the flange rubbing, right?

sentences.tagged: But most researchers say it is the tread, sliding sideways, sticking and slipping so fast that the whole wheel rings like a bell.

sentences.text: On tight curves, the flange does the hard work.

sentences.text: But how hard can you push it?

sentences.text: More than a century ago, an engineer named Nadal worked that out.

sentences.text: Once the sideways push gets roughly as big as the weight on that wheel, a typical flange can climb up and over the rail.
sentences.tagged: Once the sideways push gets roughly as big as the weight on that wheel, a typical flange can climb up and over the rail.

sentences.text: That is one way a train comes off the track.

sentences.text: And here is the twist.
sentences.tagged: And here is the twist.

sentences.text: The cone that keeps your train centered also makes it sway.
sentences.tagged: The cone that keeps your train centered also makes it sway.

sentences.text: If you push the axle to one side, the cone steers it back.
sentences.tagged: If you push the axle to one side, the cone steers it back.

sentences.text: But does it stop in the middle, where you want it?
sentences.tagged: But does it stop in the middle, where you want it?

sentences.text: It overshoots, and steers back again.
sentences.tagged: It overshoots, and steers back again.

sentences.text: If you watched from above, you would see the axle snake along the track in a smooth wave.
sentences.tagged: If you watched from above, you would see the axle snake along the track in a smooth wave.

sentences.text: Railway engineers call it hunting, and you can see why.

sentences.text: George Stephenson knew about this sway about two hundred years ago.

sentences.text: In eighteen eighty-three, an engineer called Klingel worked out how long each wave is.
sentences.tagged: In eighteen eighty-three, an engineer called Klingel worked out how long each wave is.

sentences.text: For the textbook wheelset you just saw, about seventeen meters.
sentences.tagged: For the textbook wheelset you just saw, about seventeen meters.

sentences.text: At a hundred and sixty kilometers an hour, if it kept going, that would be about two and a half sways every second.
sentences.tagged: At a hundred and sixty kilometers an hour, if it kept going, that would be about two and a half sways every second.

sentences.text: So why isn't your train always swaying like that?
sentences.tagged: So why isn't your train always swaying like that?

sentences.text: Because below a certain speed, called the critical speed, each sway is smaller than the last, and it dies away.
sentences.tagged: Because below a certain speed, called the critical speed, each sway is smaller than the last, and it dies away.

sentences.text: Above it, each sway is bigger than the last, until the flanges hammer the rails.

sentences.text: Fast trains have a fix.

sentences.text: They use flatter cones.

sentences.text: And holding each axle stiffly in its frame keeps it pointing straight.

sentences.text: But that same stiffness makes it harder to turn into a curve.

sentences.text: See the trade-off?
sentences.tagged: See the trade-off?

sentences.text: A steeper cone, or a looser axle, takes tight curves better.
sentences.tagged: A steeper cone, or a looser axle, takes tight curves better.

sentences.text: A flatter cone, or a stiffer axle, stays calm at speed.
sentences.tagged: A flatter cone, or a stiffer axle, stays calm at speed.

sentences.text: No single design is best at both.
sentences.tagged: No single design is best at both.

sentences.text: So the next time you hear that screech on a bend, you will know what it means.
